title: Bare Wafer Inspection - Contamination Detection on C205 Broadband Plasma
subtitle: Post-Planarization Quality Validation for 45nm Node Manufacturing
author: Robert Kim

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the C205 Broadband Plasma system to detect and classify Contamination defects during post-planarization inspection at the 45nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 12 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Contamination defects that are critical to yield at the 45nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the C205 Broadband Plasma platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: C205 Broadband Plasma
- Inspection Type: Bare Wafer Inspection
- Target Defect: Contamination
- Process Step: Post-Planarization
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 45nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 12

This test case applies to all C205 Broadband Plasma systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 12 for post-planarization monitoring in the 45nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: C205 Broadband Plasma
Software Version: v13.3.438
Recipe: BARE_WAFER_INSPECTION_45nm_POST_PLANARIZATION
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Low (189 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the C205 Broadband Plasma system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Bare Wafer Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Contamination defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 45nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 106 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 92% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.3% for Bare Wafer Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.98 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-06-01
Wafers Tested: 38
Total Defects Found: 3602
Defect Density: 509.58 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 1.8%
Capture Rate: 85.7%
Test Duration: 300 minutes
System Uptime: 98.2%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The C205 Broadband Plasma demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Contamination at the 45nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) SECS/GEM communication was verified with zero packet loss during data transfer.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
